title: Sounds and spelling: check yourself
intro: 10 tasks: stress, special letters, accents and question marks.

items.explanation: Ciudad ends in d, a consonant that is not n or s, so the last syllable is stressed.
optionNotes: The first of two syllables is stressed only when the word ends in a vowel, n or s.
Every word has one strong syllable.

items.prompt: Which word needs a written accent? It is stressed on the last syllable: ca-FE (coffee).
items.explanation: Cafe ends in a vowel, so the rule would put the stress on CA-. To stress the last syllable, it needs an accent: café.
optionNotes: ME-sa follows the rule: it ends in a vowel.
ho-TEL follows the rule: it ends in l.
LU-nes follows the rule: it ends in s.

items.prompt: In which word does the letter sound like “ny” in canyon?
optionNotes: Ll sounds like y in yes.
N without the tilde is a normal n.
G before e is a breathy sound from the throat.

items.context: Spain is a big country, and the year has twelve months.
items.text: Espa{{1}}a es grande. Un a{{2}}o tiene doce meses.
items.explanation: España and año are written with ñ. Ano, with n, is a different word.
Question words have a written accent: ¿Cómo te llamas?

items.prompt: One letter can change the word. Match each word with its meaning.
items.explanation: Rr is rolled and r between vowels is a tap: perro and pero are different words. The accent changes the stress: pa-PÁ (dad) and PA-pa (potato).

items.prompt: Write the Spanish word for “hello” (remember the silent letter at the start): ___
items.explanation: Hola is written with h, even though the h is silent.
Hola starts with a silent h; José has an accent on the last syllable.
The written accent shows the stressed syllable: te-LÉ-fo-no.
optionNotes: The written accent is on the second syllable, not the first.
Without the accent the rule would say -fo-, but the accent overrides the rule.
The word ends in a vowel; nothing points to the last syllable.

items.explanation: The question word comes first, then te and the verb. The question marks frame the sentence.
